title: Khotan, the jade river
place: Khotan oasis, about 1273: orchards, cotton fields, and jade gathered from the river (Polo, Book 1 ch. 36-37).

accuracy.source: Marco Polo, Travels, Yule-Cordier ed. (Project Gutenberg #10636); Claude with ChatGPT (text only), 2026-11-26
findings: Polo: Cotan has cotton, vineyards and gardens.
Polo's river 'Jasper and Chalcedony' is jade (Yule): water-rolled stones fished from the Karakash and Yurungkash rivers at Khotan, white to green.

cells.action: The caravan reaches the green oasis after the desert, on the near bank of a wide shallow river drawn with clear banks, pebbles and a few ripple lines; poplars, vineyards and cotton fields along the far bank.
In the middle of the river, three jade gatherers wade knee-deep (the water line across their knees), feeling for stones with their feet; ripples around their legs; the far bank small behind.
Close-up from above: wet hands lift a rounded river pebble of jade out of the water; only the water surface with ripples and pebbles under it fills the background (no trees).
Marco crouches on the pebbly river bank, the water at his feet, turning a piece of jade in his fingers, fascinated.
